name: Rotated surface code with aligned d=4 hole lattice

provenance.construction: Rotated surface code (checkerboard of unit-square X/Z plaquettes, weight-2 boundary checks) on a 30 x 32 grid with single-plaquette holes: X plaquettes removed at Chebyshev spacing 4 (columns 4..24, rows 0..28 step 4) and Z plaquettes at (columns 0..28, rows 3..27 step 4), the period-4 lattice aligned so the 3-wide hole-free strips next to the edges where each string type terminates fall into the lattice gaps. Each removed plaquette is one logical qubit and a weight-4 logical; logical strings between holes have weight >= 4, so d = 4 (checked exactly by enumerating all connected supports of size <= 3). Simulated annealing over boundary checks and occupancy then trimmed three boundary qubits (n 960 -> 957, k = 105 unchanged). Single layer, every check inside one unit square: r = sqrt(2), g = k d^2 / n = 1.7555.
